goal: Avoid counting one observed end screen/rare monster as both an independent exact-hint Evidence outcome and a categorical setting-likelihood outcome.

observations.eligibleEvent: One distinct screen actually shown at the end of 冒険RUSH or 超冒険RUSH.
observations.counting: One record per actual final result; do not count the same ended AT twice after a comeback/replay. Category count is one of the seven observed screens.
observations.denominator: Sum of all seven observed categories, if the interface provides complete observations; never use total game count or AT game count as the number of end screens.
observations.proposal: Use a single canonical category-count input. Derive deterministic setting constraints from matching categories in this same count vector; apply its categorical likelihood once, never add an independent Evidence hint probability. Keep category meaning visible in UI.
observations.unresolved: Confirm that every displayed AT-end screen belongs to these seven and that repeated displays after resurrection are uniquely handled by user-visible UI semantics. Require denominator and interaction specification reviewed before enabling likelihood.

observations.eligibleEvent: A distinguishable appearance of ネクロマンティス / ダークキメラ / ピットデーモン / グランキャンドロス while in a monster battle during AT.
observations.counting: Increment exactly one of four concrete monster categories per eligible appearance. Ordinary other monsters are excluded from the *conditional* denominator.
observations.denominator: Sum of the four rare-monster counts only; do not use all monster battles or all enemy appearances.
observations.proposal: One conditional categorical input model, with its Evidence count display sourced from the same records; avoid independent probability and Evidence counters. Preserve non-rare enemies as excluded unless a separately sourced baseline rate exists.
observations.unresolved: Independently verify whether these 4 percentages are conditional on all four appearances and whether in-game recording can be complete; do not infer occurrence of rare monsters from the conditional shares.

commonGeneratorValidatorRequirements: Use one observation identity per machine+trialUniverse+event; numeric and Evidence UI must refer to the same storage counts and not separately increment evidence and likelihood.
Require exact one-to-one map of numeric category labels to reviewed Evidence categories, including semantic type and setting constraints.

At research/promotion stages reject any explicit mirrored candidate until the canonical shared-input route is approved and implemented. Missing mirror metadata must not silently authorize an independent route.
Apply each single observation's setting-conditional likelihood at most once; derived constraints from deterministic category outcomes must not multiply a second independent likelihood.
Do not turn per-event conditional information gain times 200 into a 7000G selection score without actual eligible-trial exposure at the benchmark.
Require all candidate setting rows from the same source's explicitly rounded exhaustive category distributions; normalization must not invent unknown residual categories.
Until end-to-end runtime and QA checks pass, keep numericRouteStatus=PENDING_* and Research not promoted.
testsToImplementBeforePromotion: Record one AT screen and verify a single categorical likelihood update plus corresponding derived constraint (no second Evidence likelihood).
Verify a 4-monster eligible count of 1 excludes all other observed enemies from its denominator.
Disallow category counts with missing/unrecognized outcome labels; require one category per result.
Rebuild contract and runtime from the same source snapshot deterministically; ensure round-trip saved counts keep category identity.
Verify that two numeric findings cannot both mirror one Evidence ID and that erased mirror declarations fail promotion.
notes: This is a research-only design proposal, not a change to canonical UI/runtime contracts. Final observability and statistical assumptions remain unresolved.
